name: Uzbekistan
summary: Light blue, white and green horizontal bands separated by thin red stripes, with a white crescent and twelve stars in the upper hoist. It was adopted shortly after independence in 1991.
origin: Uzbekistan declared independence from the Soviet Union on 31 August 1991. The Supreme Council adopted the new flag on 18 November 1991, replacing the flag of the Uzbek SSR.

colors.name: Light blue
colors.meaning: The sky and water; also the colour of Timur's (Tamerlane's) banner.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The vital force that flows in all living things.

symbols.name: Crescent
symbols.description: A white crescent in the blue band.
symbols.meaning: The rebirth of the independent republic; also a symbol associated with Islam.

symbols.name: Twelve stars
symbols.description: Twelve white stars in rows of three, four and five.
symbols.meaning: The twelve months of the year and the constellations of the zodiac; also linked to the historic regions of Uzbekistan.

facts: The stars are arranged in rows of three, four and five, from top to bottom.
The twelve stars also allude to the ancient astronomy of Central Asia, practised in the observatory of Ulugh Beg in Samarkand.
clues: Light blue, white and green bands with red edging, a white crescent and twelve stars.
Its twelve stars stand for months and the zodiac.
Its blue was the colour of a 14th-century conqueror's banner.
